b.x: 01 On the street, do your clothes and bag match the neighborhood — or advertise a tactical hobby / a brand that is too loud? I pass as one more person. No patch, no molle, no shouting logo. Almost. One detail still shouts (shoes, pack, cap). You could find me in the middle of the sidewalk.
02 How do you use the phone while moving? One earbud, screen off the crosswalk, I watch the street. I sometimes cross while reading. I know it is dumb. Two earbuds, screen the whole way.
03 When you enter a place, do you notice the exits? Yes. It became a five-second reflex. In a new place, yes. In the usual one, no. Only when someone mentions a fire.

04 Who knows what you store and what you think about a crisis? Close family and at most one useful neighbor. No post. I have already said too much in a chat or at a bar table. I post, tag, show the kit.
05 Home–work–school: are the routes always the same? I have two and a point B. I use both. I know a shortcut, but I have not taught the family. One route, on autopilot, every day.
06 If the lights drop tonight, what can you put a hand on in two minutes? Torch, water, folder, meds. Already in place. Torch yes. The rest I know which room it is in. The phone. Then I will see.
07 The three-day pack: does it actually exist? Packed, near the door, reviewed this season. A mental list. Still need to gather it. It is still a video I watched.
08 Vehicle (if you use one): what would a stranger read on the back seat? Nothing. Kit in the trunk, closed, ordinary. A mess, but no kit on display. A sticker, a radio, a molle pack, loose papers.
09 Can you climb three flights with the pack — for real? Yes. I walk enough that it is not theater. With effort. I need to train the basics. The pack weighs more than the legs accept.
10 Does the family (or you, if you live alone) have a written point B? Written, agreed, with an out-of-city contact. We spoke once. Nobody would find the paper. I will improvise at the time.
